about.title: Parlier Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Parlier residents rely on a small network of local clinics and nearby Fresno County hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency care. When a provider misses a clear warning sign, misreads a test, or makes an error during treatment, the harm can follow a patient for years. California's MICRA law shapes how these cases move forward: a qualified medical expert typically has to review the case, and strict notice and filing deadlines apply from the moment the injury is discovered. We don't practice law ourselves — we review medical malpractice claims for Parlier residents. Our team can look at the medical records, explain whether the case meets California's malpractice standard, and walk through next steps. A poor outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice, so an early review matters. If you or a family member were harmed by a provider's error, reaching out sooner rather than later can help preserve your options.

items.title: We Understand MICRA's Tight Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so we move quickly to review your case.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into the Process
items.desc: Because California almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, we know how to line up that review early rather than waiting until it's too late to matter.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Risk to You
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. Our initial case review costs nothing, regardless of how your claim turns out.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Parlier?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines are easy to miscalculate, it helps to have us review your specific timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: My treatment in Parlier just didn't go the way I hoped — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires more than a bad outcome; it generally requires showing a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and caused the harm. A qualified medical expert typically needs to weigh in on that question, which is part of why an early case review matters.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes. California's MICRA law places a cap on non-economic damages — things like pain and suffering — though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally handled separately and aren't subject to that same cap.
